description: Work, energy methods, power, conservation principles, and motion in vertical circular systems
note: Do not treat this as a separate chapter. It is not a collection of formulas. It is a framework. Mechanics, at its core, is about tracking how energy flows through a system. Instead of focusing on forces and motion at every instant, shift perspective: Where is the energy? How is it being transferred? Is it being conserved, transformed, or dissipated? Work is simply the mechanism of energy transfer. In systems dominated by conservative forces, energy continuously transforms between potential and kinetic forms. It remains within the system, just changing its representation. Nothing is lost. In the presence of non-conservative forces, energy is no longer fully recoverable. A part of it leaves the system, typically as heat. That loss is what you account for. Most problems reduce to identifying this flow correctly. So instead of memorizing isolated results, observe the system as a whole. Track energy, and the solution often reveals itself with less effort than force-based analysis.
